chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), when he rose at the end of the night, would raise his voice until the people of the house could hear, and he would say:

O Allah, assist me upon the terror of the emergence (of the Day of Judgment), and expand for me the narrowness of the bed (grave), and grant me the goodness that is before death, and grant me the goodness that is after death.

key_terms.خَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَ الْمَوْتِ: the goodness that is after death
key_terms.خَيْرَ مَا قَبْلَ الْمَوْتِ: the goodness that is before death
key_terms.ضِيقُ الْمَضْجَعِ: the narrowness of the bed (referring to the grave)
key_terms.هَوْلُ الْمُطَّلَعِ: the terror/awe of the emergence (of the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What was the supplication of Imam al-Sadiq (as) when waking up at the end of the night?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s vocal devotion during Tahajjud, serving as a pedagogical model for the family to internalize the reality of death. The supplication specifically addresses the transition from the 'narrowness' of the grave (Qabr) to the 'awe' of the final resurrection, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preparing for the Hereafter through conscious, audible remembrance.
